newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs easier due to slight rise in share prices.
newsitem.headline: JGBs easier due to slight rise in share prices.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures were easier in thin, quiet trade by midday on Thursday due to a rise in share prices.
"Nothing is happening right now. Trade is very thin," said a trader for a foreign brokerage house.

JGBs were stuck in a narrow range, capped on the upside due to an oversupply of corporate bonds, and supported on the downside by investors' demand for cash bonds on dips, said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
In the afternoon session, there would be some focus on May machinery orders data due at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT), traders said.
The September stood at 124.76, down slightly from the previous day's close of 124.84. Turnover was 13,332 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.305 percent as of 0232 GMT, up from Wednesday's close of 2.3 percent.
Although the market is suffering from a dearth of fresh trading incentives, the May machinery orders data is not likely to be able to fill that void, traders said.

"The market will, of course, pay attention to release of an indicator, but machinery orders usually come in near expectations, and there won't be much effect unless there is a large deviation," the second trader said.
Traders said the market expects machinery orders in May to have increased by six to seven percent month-on-month.
"A double-digit increase would be considered much higher than expectations and probably invite some selling," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.

Even a larger-than-expected increase, however, is unlikely to trigger sharp falls, as investors are waiting in the wings to pick up cash bonds on dips, a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
"We may see some fun action, if JGBs fall due to a larger-than-expected increase," the trader said.
Japan's private-sector machinery orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, rose a seasonally adjusted 7.2 percent in April month-on-month.

The upside was heavy this morning, due to lacklusture sales of Tokyo Electric Power Co and Chugoku Electric Power Co's 3.225 percent 20-year straight bonds launched on Wednesday, the second trader said.
"It is not enough of a factor to cause JGBs to fall sharply, but it is making the upside heavy," the trader said.
